title: Chapter 1137
paragraphs: Chapter 1137
Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (6)
Why can only the Valeria Hister of the 677th dimension not coexist with me in one world? Why, when I first fell into the dimensional passage, was I in the farthest place from the 677th dimension?
Could it be that all of this is because she and I are the same person? The me of the past, and the me of now. Because the past and the present cannot exist together.
"Haha..."
It wasn't easy to accept.

If the common sense that the past and present cannot coexist applies, then what about all the other paradoxes I've experienced so far? Why are they so inexplicably complex, while only a simple, clear order applies to me and the Valeria of the 677th dimension?
But there was nothing I could do about that problem. On the other hand, I had many other things to do.
I had to save Jin and prevent the entire world from falling into the hands of the Demon Army. From the beginning, I had said we should turn back time for that very reason.

I wasn't the only one who was lonely and in pain. I wasn't the only one who was wronged. All the Valerias, all the people who had fallen while resisting the Zipples, while resisting the Demon Army, must have been in just as much pain.
A record that Jin had just liberated Lafrarosa was floating up in the window.
I sent her a message.
Starting with the sentence
"Let's find a way to intervene directly in the 677th dimension... Even if coexistence is impossible, I have to help Jin in some way."

Too many parts of the history of the 677th dimension had been changed by Jin. I had also discovered a record that the Demon Army had begun to pay serious attention to the 677th dimension, so I needed to hurry.
Everything depended on me and Jin. And us. That much was an unchanging fact.
While searching for a way to intervene in the 677th dimension, I also continued to try to enter directly in my spare time.
And then I found just one place, a space where I could step in myself.
It was the very subspace where Solderet and I had examined the records of the Demon Army before turning back time.
"This place isn't classified as the 677th dimension in the first place. Which means it corresponds to a dimensional passage..."
Still, it was the dimensional passage closest to the 677th dimension. In my recording window, more of the events happening in the 677th dimension were being recorded than ever before.
"So you, like me, were cast out into the dimensional passage instead of having your time turned back."
Since Solderet had turned back time from this place, it also felt like I had returned to the starting point.
"Is this... a gate? Was there something like this?"
A pure white, massive gate.

Clearly, before the world had regressed, Solderet and I had never made such a gate. But I knew instinctively that this was the legacy Solderet had left behind. Just as Solderet was still helping Jin in the form of power, what was left in this subspace was also an authority he had left behind.
When I looked into the records about the gate, it was true. Beyond this gate was the authority Solderet had left behind as he realized what he was in his final moments.
There was light.
A light that felt as if I could fight the Kelliark Zipfel of the 33rd dimension as much as I wanted, if I obtained it.
I felt that the reason I had wandered the dimensional passage all this time was for this very thing. At the same time, a wave of fear surged up.
'With Temar's body and Barisada... anyone can enter this space without Solderet's permission. And if they use the dimensional passage, they can enter even without them.'

Was there another dimension where Temar's body remained? There was one Barisada per dimension, but what about...? If the Demon Army learned of the existence of this legacy, they would never just leave this power be.
And since I had entered this space, the pursuers would eventually find this place someday. Because the Origin Stones of each dimension were constantly digging into my whereabouts.
In that sense, this legacy was a double-edged sword.
'I have to put a seal on the subspace and the gate, and guide Jin to reach here before the Demon Army. Now... I'm really almost there.'
The Kelliark Zipfel of the 33rd dimension invaded the 677th dimension even faster than I had expected.
Fortunately, the events that had occurred in the 677th dimension were appearing more and more clearly on my recording window.
"...If it weren't for the variable that is Malugia, it would have been the end."

Of course, it was true that the variable had a significant effect thanks to the Vamel Alliance showing that much strength. But if Kelliark recovered and returned, it seemed they wouldn't be able to hold out then.
His wounds must have been deep. He didn't show himself until the Vamel Alliance went to the Black Sea, and until the white fleet led by Rondo Zipfel invaded the 677th dimension.
From around that time, I was receiving records of the battlefield in almost real-time. And for the first time, my messages also began to arrive at the desired moments.
I don't know how desperately I cheered for the Vamel Alliance.
I couldn't send a message every moment because of the Demon Army's pursuit. The strength of the Vamel Alliance was also not so lacking that I had to keep sending messages.
"Please, please just hold on a little longer...!"
Those trying to protect the world, those who rushed at the enemy without sparing their lives, those who sacrificed to save people, those who did not fall.
I felt so sorry for them it was driving me mad. If possible, if only I could, I wanted to run to the battlefield right now and fight alongside them.
But my battle had started here, not in the Black Sea.
'A pursuer!'
It was a point in time when there was truly not much time left until the Vamel Alliance released the curse on Temar's left arm. I had to protect this place at all costs.
I immediately went out of the seal and lured the enemies to another area of the dimensional passage. The pursuer was Silyn Zipfel, and her three direct subordinate Genesis Knight mages.
That wasn't enough to catch me. I was someone who had reached a state where I could create matter with magic.
Normally, that would have been the case.

But the fact that I had to conserve my power held me back. I was in the process of preparing a magic that could stop the world's time for Jin at a critical moment, and because of that, I couldn't fully concentrate on the battle.
"Heok, heok..."
Still, I succeeded in making the enemies retreat. I had thrown the three mages into the labyrinth of the dimensional passage, and I had shaken off Silyn.
However, there was no time to heal my wounds with the light of the dimensional passage. This time, the injuries were so deep that the healing power of the light alone wouldn't be enough.
When I returned to the legacy and checked the recording window, an endlessly bleak war situation was described.
The content that Kelliark, who had awakened and become an even more terrible monster, was massacring Jin and his people was being updated without rest.
I couldn't let Jin die.

I squeezed out all my remaining power and stopped the time of the battlefield, excluding Jin, Ameris, and Lokia. I had used my one and only chance to directly exert my influence on the 677th dimension.
I don't know if it was the most opportune moment or not. I just lost consciousness, hoping for success.
It was a success.
When I opened my eyes, I met Jin. I was able to come to my senses after receiving a little of his magic.
How could I describe that moment? The person I had wanted to see so much, even from before time was turned back... the one and only person I had chosen was looking at me.
What should I say to the person I had waited for, crossing countless dimensions as if crossing between stars, wandering endlessly through the empty dimensional passage?
He was disappointed in me.
I wasn't hurt. Even if it were me, if someone had chosen me as they pleased to change the world... I would have felt the same. No matter how right it was.
Still, the ten-odd minutes I spent heading to the white gate, carried on his back, was a warm moment that would never come again in my life.
To the point where even if the world were to end in that time, I would have wanted to stay like this for even a moment longer...
Jin.
Jin... I...
Jin embraced the fallen Valeria.
"Valeria... Valeria."
Jin was realizing the reason why she had felt so familiar the moment he first saw her.
This person is my master.
The very person who saved me in my past life. When time was turned back, that person, with all her memories intact like me... was exiled to the dimensional passage.
And yet, she didn't give up and came this far. In a time of endless darkness that could be called an eon, she endured an unknown future and came to find me.
And he had spoken to such a person as if questioning her, asking why she couldn't have prepared a better future, if this was the best she could do.
Valeria was smiling as she looked at Jin.
"I'm glad. I was able to create the memories for you."
"I... had forgotten everything. I'm sorry, Valeria. I had forgotten everything..."
Don't forget us then. Don't forget all of this. Jin remembered the memory Valeria had engraved on him before Solderet had turned back time and met her eyes.
Valeria was smiling, showing her white teeth.
"Jin, let's go now."
The white gate where Solderet had left the power of light.
Because he had read the memories, he knew. Valeria had examined the white gate with her recording magic and had learned everything about the power of light.
The moment Jin obtained that power, this space would collapse. If that happened, she would disappear. Because she could not exist with the Valeria of the 677th dimension.
"If I do that, you'll..."
"It's my limit anyway, even if this space doesn't disappear. You know..."
Valeria's arms wrapped around Jin's neck. She kissed his cheek and patted his back.
"Jin, I have saved my Jin Runcandel."
So you save your Valeria Hister.
Save our world.
His throat was choked, and no answer came.
He nodded, his eyes squeezed shut. In the end, Jin carried Valeria on his back again.
"Let's go, Jin. Carry me."
He began to walk towards the white gate. One step, two steps. As he moved towards the light beyond the gate, he felt his back getting lighter and lighter.

"The present, the past, and the future are connected somewhere. That's why we can feel each other's warmth now, crossing that tangled time. It must be the same for death and life. Jin, remember. This is something we did. Take care of... me. The people... I couldn't protect in any world, please take care of them."
In the blinding light, Valeria's voice was fading.
